title: John Healey appointed Chancellor amid property tax speculation
summary:
John Healey has been appointed as the new Chancellor of the Exchequer in Prime Minister Andy Burnham's cabinet, replacing Rachel Reeves. Speculation has intensified around potential property tax reforms, including a Land Value Tax system.

title: US and Gulf buyers account for 55% of London ultra-prime sales
summary:
Buyers from the United States and Gulf states accounted for 55% of London's ultra-prime property transactions above £15 million in the first half of 2026. The 34 deals totalled £1.24 billion, up from £694.1 million across 27 transactions in the same period of 2025.

title: Major lenders raise mortgage rates amid geopolitical tensions
summary:
Halifax, HSBC and Barclays have increased mortgage rates by up to 0.2% following a sharp rise in swap rates driven by geopolitical tensions in Iran. The changes, which affect fixed rate products for homemovers and first-time buyers, come as Andy Burnham takes office as Prime Minister.

title: Rayner returns as housing secretary under new PM Burnham
summary:
Angela Rayner has been reappointed as Housing Secretary following Andy Burnham's appointment as Prime Minister. The move comes after Steve Reed departed the role, having served less than a year since his appointment in September 2025.

title: Dunstone ownership changes at Purplebricks parent Strike
summary:
Changes to the ownership structure of Purplebricks parent company Strike have emerged following Companies House filings, alongside overdue annual accounts for both entities. Charles Dunstone is no longer listed personally as a person of significant control, with his investment vehicle Freston Ventures now holding that position.

title: Property industry urges Burnham to prioritise housing reform
summary:
Andy Burnham has become Prime Minister and immediately faced calls from the property sector to address housing market challenges. Industry bodies have outlined priorities including transaction reform, stamp duty review and infrastructure investment to support the government's 1.5 million homes target.

title: Selby estate agency transfers to employee ownership
summary:
Jigsaw, a family-run estate and letting agency based in Selby, has transferred ownership of the business to its employees through an Employee Ownership Trust. The transition follows more than two decades of operation since the firm was established in 2001.

title: UK auction volumes rise 35% as landlords offload stock
summary:
UK property auction volumes increased by 35.3% in June compared to the previous year, with 4,008 lots offered and total funds raised climbing to £519.7 million. The increase in stock outpaced buyer demand, resulting in the national success rate declining to 65.3%, according to Essential Information Group data.

title: Birmingham uses Airbnb data to tackle social housing fraud
summary:
Birmingham City Council has begun comparing its social housing records with Airbnb listings to identify properties being advertised without permission. The programme follows a recent agreement between the Cabinet Office and Airbnb aimed at identifying social housing tenants who illegally sublet their properties.
